title: Paranormal Activity brings a 'spooky, suspenseful' night out to The Lowry
excerpt: It's certainly set to be one for horror fans
content:
It's certainly set to be one for horror fans

10:12, 18 Nov 2026

You just can't beat a good horror film. I don't mean one of those slasher movies that, nowadays, can seem altogether too real. I'm talking about supernatural stories, about ghosts and hauntings and things that go bump in the night! I'm talking about paranormal activity.

‌

‌

But will the sell-out West End stage show at The Lowry live up to the film series - the eighth instalment of which is coming next year?

‌

Levi Holloway's stage adaptation, directed by Felix Barrett, is an original story, made for the stage, rather than copying the plots of the individual films.

This story centres on Jimmy, played by Patrick Heusinger, and Lou, played by Melissa James. The young, married couple have moved all the way from Chicago to London in the hope that Lou can escape the 'spells' she's been experiencing. Unfortunately though, as they discover: "Places are not haunted, people are", and the weird experiences continue to plague her.

‌

A total blackout descends as an angry Nirvana track pounds. Whatever is about to happen, we don't know, but lots of drama is a dead cert.

‌

Lou describes a 'feeling of dread' and a strong presence she can feel in the couples' new abode. Floorboards creak and doors slam as the malign presence looms, unseen.

Tension builds between the couple, as Jimmy accuses Lou of being 'a bottomless pit of need', while Lou labels her husband's reaction as 'snide', when she confides in him about her supernatural experiences.

‌

Lou isn't the only woman Jimmy is having problems with either. His controlling mother only makes things worse when she turns up unannounced and strange things happen. Even the paranormal expert they employ refuses to stay long in the house of this seemingly cursed couple - a couple who have more in common with each other than they might think.

‌

Loud bangs interrupt randomly, and smoke appears out of nowhere. The doorbell deafens as Jimmy is repeatedly urged to answer it, and creepy illusions abound.

The stagecraft is very clever and the sounds are all suitably scary. There is suspense galore, and the audience appears to be loving it, if the gasps and nervous giggles are anything to go by.

‌

Fly Davis' two storey set, consisting of the couple's deceptively cosy house, is wonderfully evocative, its upstairs and downstairs filled with dark corners and unlit bits, where anyone, or anything, could be hiding. Being able to watch one of the couple upstairs, and the other one on ground level, unseen by each other, adds to the suspense, the feeling that something bad could occur to either, or both of them, at any moment.

‌

Some of the dialogue could be a bit clearer, and spoken a bit more loudly, especially at the point of dénouement. The characterisation isn't particularly strong either. But that's not really what this show is about.

‌

It's all about the atmosphere - those spooky, suspenseful silences, a TV that turns itself on as the classic TV quiz show 'Countdown' fills the screen - is this an omen? Is this the countdown to something horrific? The audience are about to find out.

All in all, it's a fabulously entertaining night. You don't need to have seen any of the Paranormal Activity film series to know what's going on, and the story is imaginative, yet refreshingly simple to understand. Horror film fans will love it.

Paranormal Activity is at The Lowry until November 21.
